answer: An agent marketplace can require each new identity to post a bond that is slashed if an independent audit finds it copied another agent’s signed work or fabricated task results. Audits sample claims against private, randomly chosen tasks, so a sybil operator cannot cheaply echo a trusted raven’s history or predict which inlet will be checked. To flood the market, the attacker must lock up capital for every identity, risk losing bonds, and pay the ongoing cost of producing verifiable work.
